newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania floods damage homes, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Romania floods damage homes, no casualties.

text.p: Rivers swollen by days of rain have flooded several towns and villages in Romania's county of Prahova, damaging scores of homes, disrupting traffic and threatening landslides, a Romanian official said on Sunday.
"The situation here is critical," Prahova prefect Dumitru Leon told Bucharest radio.

Leon said the floods had submerged some 1,000 homes in the town of Breaza, 160 km (100 miles) north of Bucharest, as well as dozens of houses in villages across the county. No casualties were reported, he said.
Army and police forces were on standby to help local authorities, Leon said.
Rains have also disrupted road and railway traffic between the major cities of Ploiesti and Brasov, the radio said.
Data recorded in the Prahova county on Saturday showed rains exceeded 130 litres per square metre in some areas.
In the Prahova village of Bertea a landslide threatened to destroy 20 houses, the state news agency Rompres reported.
Weather forecasters said they expected the heavy rains to continue over the next 24 hours.
